evidence: packages/grafana-runtime/src/config.ts:97 declares `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined;` with no annotation. tsconfig.json:8 has strict:true, so strictNullChecks is on and the property's type is `undefined`, not `number | undefined` (packages/grafana-data/src/types/config.ts:200). `implements GrafanaConfig` still compiles, because `undefined` is assignable to `number | undefined`, so this is not a build break. But anyone reading `config.anonymousDeviceLimit` gets type `undefined`, even though `merge(this, defaults, options)` (config.ts ~line 191) fills in the number sent by the backend (pkg/api/dtos/frontend_settings.go:195, int64). One-line fix: `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined = undefined;`.

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:109-118 runs CountDevices in one session, then the INSERT ... ON CONFLICT upsert at :149-153 runs in a separate session, with no transaction or lock. Concurrent first requests from different new devices, or from several Grafana instances, can all see count < limit and all insert, so the limit can be overshot. The localCache in impl.go only dedupes the same device ID on one instance. The race is real, but the result is a soft overshoot of a usage limit, not data corruption. Making it strict would need a transactional or locking design.

updateDevice (database.go:73-103) is private and only called from database.go:115-116, after count >= deviceLimit. There, zero rows affected means the device is not among the active devices in the 30-day window, i.e. it is a new or expired device that would push past the limit. Refusing it with ErrDeviceLimitReached is exactly the intended behavior, and client.go uses that error to deny access. Zero rows on MySQL when values are unchanged is not a concern either: the connection string sets clientFoundRows=true (pkg/services/sqlstore/sqlstore.go:287), so matched rows are counted.

`anonymousDeviceExpiration = 30 * 24 * time.Hour` is defined in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:16 and again in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/api/api.go:18. A third copy, `thirtyDays`, is in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:25 and is used by usageStatFn. All three define the same 'active device' window, so they could drift apart. Exporting one constant from anonstore (already imported by api and impl) would fix it. This is maintainability only; the values match today.

In production, device.UpdatedAt is set to time.Now() in TagDevice (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go ~line 140), only microseconds before CreateOrUpdateDevice calls time.Now() for the count window (database.go:110). Both windows are 30 days wide with a 1-minute slack at the end (database.go:81 and :110), so a sub-second gap has no practical effect. The only case where they differ by much is a test that sets UpdatedAt artificially.

TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database_test.go:51-70) only checks that a second, new device is rejected. The success path of updateDevice (database.go:73-103) is never tested: updating an already-registered device after the limit is reached. That path decides whether existing anonymous users keep access once the limit is hit (client.go returns the error and fails authentication), and its BETWEEN window logic is new and non-trivial. The test should call CreateOrUpdateDevice again with the original device ID and assert NoError.

The existing TestIntegrationAnonStore_DeleteDevicesOlderThan (database_test.go:19-24), from before this PR, also leaves CreatedAt unset and inserts through the same upsert on all DB integration backends. The new test builds its device the same way (database_test.go:55-60). A zero time.Time just stores a zero timestamp in the created_at column, and nothing in the limit logic reads CreatedAt (the count and update both filter on updated_at, database.go:78, :161). No constraint or default-value problem results.
